sub_service: Septic tank desludging, vehicle-pass system, illegal-dumping enforcement, pit-latrine conversion
problem_type: Septic tank full/needs desludging, illegal septage dumping, non-compliant pit/twin-pit/hanging latrine
department: Health / Engineering Wing, Kochi Municipal Corporation
authority: Health Officer / Executive Engineer, Kochi Municipal Corporation; licensed desludging operators
description: The Kochi Municipal Corporation Septage Management Byelaw (Draft) regulates on-site sanitation systems (septic tanks, pits) citywide. It mandates septic tanks be desludged periodically (recommended interval 2-3 years), bans pit latrines, twin-pit latrines, and hanging latrines outright, and sets a fee/tariff structure for desludging carried out via the Corporation or its licensed operators: a Rs. 400/trip fee payable to the Municipal Corporation, plus a tariff of Rs. 3,000-5,000 depending on septic tank size. A vehicle-pass system (detailed in Annexures I-IV) governs which desludging vehicles may operate and where they may legally discharge septage. Illegal dumping of septage (i.e. not at a designated treatment/disposal point) draws a spot fine of Rs. 25,000. Households still using a banned pit/twin-pit/hanging latrine are eligible for a conversion subsidy of Rs. 10,000 or Rs. 15,400 (amount depends on conversion type) to shift to a compliant septic-tank system.
procedure: A household or establishment needing desludging contacts the Corporation or a licensed desludging operator, pays the applicable trip fee/tariff, and the operator obtains/carries the vehicle pass before transporting septage to a Corporation-designated disposal/treatment point. Households with a banned pit/twin-pit/hanging latrine can apply to the Corporation for the conversion subsidy to upgrade to a compliant septic-tank system.
sla: SLA NOT FOUND — the byelaw sets desludging *frequency* (recommended every 2-3 years) and fee/fine amounts, but does not state a numeric response/resolution-time SLA for a desludging request or complaint.
escalation_procedure: Illegal septage dumping (i.e. discharge outside a Corporation-designated point) is enforced with a spot fine of Rs. 25,000, levied against the vehicle operator/owner responsible for the dumping.
escalation_authority: Health Officer, Kochi Municipal Corporation (byelaw enforcement)

faq.question: How often should a septic tank be desludged?
faq.answer: The byelaw recommends desludging every 2-3 years, via the Corporation or a licensed operator holding a valid vehicle pass.

faq.question: What is the fine for illegally dumping septage instead of taking it to a designated disposal point?
faq.answer: Rs. 25,000 spot fine, levied on the vehicle operator/owner.

faq.question: I still use a pit/twin-pit/hanging latrine — what are my options?
faq.answer: These are banned under the byelaw. A conversion subsidy of Rs. 10,000 or Rs. 15,400 (depending on conversion type) is available to upgrade to a compliant septic-tank system.

citizen_guidance: Get septic tanks desludged every 2-3 years only via the Corporation or a licensed operator with a valid vehicle pass — illegal dumping draws a Rs. 25,000 spot fine. Pit, twin-pit, and hanging latrines are banned; a Rs. 10,000-15,400 Corporation subsidy is available to convert to a compliant septic-tank system.
